questions.questionText: Find the smallest number which, when increased by 2, is exactly divisible by 10, 12 and 16.
questions.explanation: Number + 2 must be a multiple of the LCM, which is 240. So the number is 240 − 2 = 238.

questions.questionText: Find the smallest number which, when increased by 2, is exactly divisible by 5, 15 and 25.
questions.explanation: Number + 2 must be a multiple of the LCM, which is 75. So the number is 75 − 2 = 73.

questions.questionText: Find the smallest number which, when increased by 2, is exactly divisible by 8, 10 and 12.
questions.explanation: Number + 2 must be a multiple of the LCM, which is 120. So the number is 120 − 2 = 118.

questions.questionText: What is the least number which leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 12 or 24?
questions.explanation: LCM of 12, 24 = 24. Least number = LCM + 2 = 26.

questions.questionText: What is the least number which leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 8, 9 or 30?
questions.explanation: LCM of 8, 9, 30 = 360. Least number = LCM + 1 = 361.

questions.questionText: What is the least number which leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 4 or 25?
questions.explanation: LCM of 4, 25 = 100. Least number = LCM + 1 = 101.

questions.questionText: What is the least number which leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 12 or 36?
questions.explanation: LCM of 12, 36 = 36. Least number = LCM + 1 = 37.

questions.questionText: Find the smallest number that leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 18 or 45, but is exactly divisible by 11.
questions.explanation: Numbers of the form 90k + 2 (LCM = 90). Try k = 1, 2, ... until divisible by 11: first success gives 902.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest 5-digit number which leaves remainder 2 when divided by 5, 12 and 20?
questions.explanation: LCM = 60. Need L·k + 2 ≥ 10000. Smallest k = 167, giving 10022.
questions.shortcut: Take the first multiple of LCM at/above the limit, add r.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest 4-digit number which leaves remainder 3 when divided by 10, 40 and 45?
questions.explanation: LCM = 360. Need L·k + 3 ≥ 1000. Smallest k = 3, giving 1083.
questions.shortcut: Take the first multiple of LCM at/above the limit, add r.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest 4-digit number which leaves remainder 2 when divided by 6, 9 and 18?
questions.explanation: LCM = 18. Need L·k + 2 ≥ 1000. Smallest k = 56, giving 1010.
questions.shortcut: Take the first multiple of LCM at/above the limit, add r.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest 4-digit number which leaves remainder 1 when divided by 6, 12 and 36?
questions.explanation: LCM = 36. Need L·k + 1 ≥ 1000. Smallest k = 28, giving 1009.
questions.shortcut: Take the first multiple of LCM at/above the limit, add r.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest 4-digit number which leaves remainder 1 when divided by 4, 15 and 25?
questions.explanation: LCM = 300. Need L·k + 1 ≥ 1000. Smallest k = 4, giving 1201.
questions.shortcut: Take the first multiple of LCM at/above the limit, add r.

questions.questionText: Find the least number which when divided by 15, 18 and 36 leaves remainders 7, 10 and 28 respectively.
questions.explanation: In each case divisor − remainder = 8, so number + 8 is divisible by all. Least = LCM − 8 = 180 − 8 = 172.

questions.questionText: Find the smallest number that leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 9 or 20, but is exactly divisible by 11.
questions.explanation: Numbers of the form 180k + 2 (LCM = 180). Try k = 1, 2, ... until divisible by 11: first success gives 902.

questions.questionText: Find the least number which when divided by 10, 36 and 45 leaves remainders 3, 29 and 38 respectively.
questions.explanation: In each case divisor − remainder = 7, so number + 7 is divisible by all. Least = LCM − 7 = 180 − 7 = 173.

questions.questionText: Find the least number which when divided by 5, 20 and 45 leaves remainders 1, 16 and 41 respectively.
questions.explanation: In each case divisor − remainder = 4, so number + 4 is divisible by all. Least = LCM − 4 = 180 − 4 = 176.

questions.questionText: Find the smallest number that leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 4 or 24, but is exactly divisible by 9.
questions.explanation: Numbers of the form 24k + 3 (LCM = 24). Try k = 1, 2, ... until divisible by 9: first success gives 27.

questions.questionText: How many numbers between 1 and 1000 (inclusive) leave a remainder of 1 when divided by 10 and by 30?
questions.explanation: Such numbers are 30k + 1. We need 30k + 1 ≤ 1000, so k runs from 0 to 33: 34 numbers.
questions.shortcut: Count terms of the AP LCM·k + r up to the limit.

questions.questionText: Find the least positive number that leaves remainder 7 when divided by 10 and remainder 17 when divided by 36.
questions.explanation: Check numbers 7, 7+10, 7+2×10, ... until the remainder on dividing by 36 is 17. First match: 17.
questions.shortcut: List numbers of the form r1 + multiple of first divisor, test the second condition.

questions.questionText: Find the least positive number that leaves remainder 22 when divided by 24 and remainder 14 when divided by 40.
questions.explanation: Check numbers 22, 22+24, 22+2×24, ... until the remainder on dividing by 40 is 14. First match: 94.
questions.shortcut: List numbers of the form r1 + multiple of first divisor, test the second condition.

questions.questionText: How many numbers between 1 and 2000 (inclusive) leave a remainder of 2 when divided by 6 and by 40?
questions.explanation: Such numbers are 120k + 2. We need 120k + 2 ≤ 2000, so k runs from 0 to 16: 17 numbers.
questions.shortcut: Count terms of the AP LCM·k + r up to the limit.
